correctness.rationale: For all 0<mu<1 and mu^2<=nu<=mu, third moment of a supported ability is bounded sharply by two Cauchy–Schwarz inequalities with unique atomic equality laws. The beta(2,2) CDF is F(x)=3x^2-2x^3, yielding D=6nu-4E(X^3)-1 and the exact attained interval. Polynomial x(4x-3)^2/8>=0 proves optimum D=9mu/4-1 at lower mean; discriminant 4mu(9mu-4) gives the full fixed-variance sign window. Uniform beta density bound 3/2 and integral 2/lambda give |D_lambda-D|<=6/lambda, so lambda>75 ensures opposite signs for the exact rational equal-moment laws. Birth-death harmonic recurrences, exact detailed-balance ratios and monotone likelihood ratio prove finite population conclusions for all integers J>=2, interior counts and the stated strictly positive parameters. Exact-Fraction checker passed current package path. Finite tests support but do not replace these universal proofs.

value.rationale: Phenotypic contest ability and win/loss rates are a natural quantity in the triggering 2025 behavioral-ecology study. The simplest unimodal nonuniform symmetric beta opponent produces a sharp underdog mean threshold 4/9 (unlike a uniform opponent, for which ability mean decides the contest); with fixed variance there is a nontrivial complete interval where opposite ecological outcomes remain possible. An explicit all-finite-noise comparison demonstrates the effect survives finite logistic discrimination, while a fully specified finite winner-replacement chain translates it to fixation and stationary occupancy for all community sizes. The fact is a motivated exact benchmark, not a claimed empirical law or a new general mathematical inequality.
